    {"name": "cabin_class", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Cabin class plausibly affects service/comfort levels received (treatment) and satisfaction expectations/ratings (outcome), making it a common cause. Not named in the query."}

  "confounders": [

    {"name": "cabin_class", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.65}
  ],
  "confounder_quality": 0.55,
  "rationale": "The added columns clearly supply candidate TREATMENTS (multiple service-quality/operational causes) whose effect on the outcome is being attributed. Two columns (traveller_segment, cabin_class) function as plausible confounders -- common causes of both the service experience received and the rating given -- and neither is named in the query, so they show some genuine causal reasoning. However, they overlap heavily with existing original columns (Type of Traveller, Class), so they are re-encodings rather than newly surfaced latent confounders, and one could argue class partly lies on the causal path. The confounder set is thin (only two, both plausibility ~0.6) relative to many treatments, and several treatments themselves risk being mediators of one another. Overall the causal setup is partially realised: treatments present, confounders present but modest in quality and originality."
}
